events.objective: Establish the true onset and scope of notification-service memory pressure: pull memory/restart metrics and logs for notification-service over the last 7 days and pinpoint exactly when OOMKilled restarts and memory growth began (compare the earlier two restarts this week vs today's). Determine whether memory rises gradually (leak/buildup) or jumps abruptly, and whether consumer lag spikes precede or follow the OOM events. Also check whether any OTHER service shows concurrent memory growth or restarts in the same window, to test whether this is notification-service-specific or a shared-component effect.

Find what changed and when across ALL services in the last 24-48h: list deployments and config changes touching notification-service AND any shared infrastructure it uses (Kafka brokers, message queue config, node/instance sizing, JVM/container limits, email provider). Pay special attention to the Kafka maintenance today -- identify exactly what was changed, when, and whether any consumer group / topic / retention / partition setting was altered. Also search historical incidents for prior notification-service OOMs or Kafka-replay OOM patterns, and map notification-service's dependencies to see what shared components it competes with for memory.

Zoom into the window around the Kafka maintenance (from the change time identified by task b through the latest OOM): examine consumer lag time series, rebalance events, partition assignment, and per-consumer fetch/throughput for notification-service's consumer group, plus heap/GC or RSS logs if available. Test specifically whether the OOM correlates with an unusually large replay volume or with a rebalance/traffic shift rather than message volume itself.

args.query: Kafka consumer replay lag spike OOM

events.statement: The only config change on shared infrastructure in the 48h window (2026-03-21→23) is a Kafka maintenance change: kafka key log.retention.ms reduced from 604800000 to 259200000 (7 days → 3 days), changed at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z by platform-team, described as 'Kafka maintenance: reduce retention to 3 days'. No topic/partition/consumer-group/rebalance setting was altered in this change.

notification-service itself was deployed on 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z (dep-5402, v3.8.0, author s.menon) with change 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering' — a ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment — and it is still live, not rolled back. This is the only recent deploy touching notification-service.

The only other deployment in the window is unrelated to Kafka/notification: auth-service v7.1.4 on 2026-03-22T13:00:00Z (ci-bot, 'bump jackson'). No rolling back is recorded on any deploy (all rolled_back_at: null).

Kafka is a SHARED component used by several services: order-service (queue-produce), payment-service (queue-produce), settlement-service (queue-consume) and notification-service (queue-consume). notification-service also depends on email-provider (external, no telemetry). So notification-service competes for the shared Kafka cluster with order-, payment- and settlement-services.

Historical precedent (lead only): HIST-104 (2025-11-05) 'notification-service lag after Kafka broker rebalance' had identical symptoms (consumer lag spike, delayed emails) but root cause 'Partition reassignment caused consumer group rebalancing storm' — an infrastructure/rebalance cause, not a retention change; resolution was 'Throttled reassignment'. A second lead HIST-112 (2026-02-03, settlement-service) is 'Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance'.

The Kafka maintenance change (retention 7d→3d) does not by itself force a data replay — lowering retention truncates old segments rather than re-reading them; the reported 'consumer choking on a replay' is not supported by any change I found (no consumer-group offset reset, no topic/partition change recorded). The only change that adds unbounded in-memory growth is the notification-service v3.8.0 template cache deployed 2 days before onset.

events.answer: Across all services in the last ~7 days there are only 3 changes: a Kafka config change (log.retention.ms 604800000→259200000, i.e. 7d→3d, 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z, platform-team), a notification-service deploy (v3.8.0, 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z, 'Add in-memory template cache', ConcurrentHashMap, not rolled back), and an unrelated auth-service patch. No topic, partition, consumer-group or retention-on-consumer setting was altered, and Kafka is shared with order-, payment- and settlement-services (and notification-service also calls an external email-provider). The 'choking on a replay' theory is not supported by the recorded change (lowering retention truncates old segments; it does not force a re-read), whereas the only change adding unbounded in-memory state is the notification-service template cache deployed two days before onset — reported as leads, not a conclusion.

events.statement: notification-service memory_pct rises gradually and monotonically within each ~24h cycle, then resets — a sawtooth, not an abrupt jump. 7-day series starts ~48% after each reset and climbs in ~5%/2h steps to ~95-98% before the next drop.

Three OOMKilled restarts of the same container notification-service-7d9f (exit code 137) occurred, timed at 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z, 2026-03-22T21:59:47Z and 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z — one per day, each ~1h earlier than the previous.

Cumulative restart counter confirms exactly 3 restarts, stepping 0→1 at the 22:00 bucket of Mar 21, 1→2 at 22:00 of Mar 22, and 2→3 at 20:00 of Mar 23; it was a flat 0 for all of Mar 20 and most of Mar 21.

Consumer lag is flat/low (~56-65 msgs) throughout each day and spikes only in the same 2h bucket as each OOM: max 17161.92 at 2026-03-21T22:00Z, max 17611.66 at 2026-03-22T20:00Z, max 18137.93 at 2026-03-23T18:00Z — i.e. lag spikes coincide with the memory-exhaustion/OOM window, not before the ~24h ramp.
order-service memory_pct is flat and stable across the whole window (avg ~59.5-60.5, max ~66), showing no concurrent memory growth like notification-service's ramp.

The lag spike is short-lived relative to the memory ramp: after each OOM the lag returns to baseline in the same 2h bucket that the restart froze (e.g. 2026-03-23T20:00Z avg 1542.68 falls back to 57.89 by 2026-03-23T22:00Z). This is consistent with lag being a consequence of the restart, not a leading trigger.

events.description: Tool budget exhausted before comparing memory_pct/restarts across the other co-tenant services (only order-service was checked; email-service is not a real service and email-provider is an external dependency with no metrics). The exact scope of a shared-component effect is therefore unverified.
Could not query kafka metrics (cpu_pct/messages_in_per_s/under_replicated_partitions) or kafka's memory; kafka exposes no memory_pct metric and the kafka query did not execute.
No metrics for the external email-provider dependency, so email delivery delay (the reported ~25 min) could not be directly measured.

events.answer: notification-service memory grows gradually and monotonically (sawtooth ~48% → ~98%), not abruptly: three OOMKilled restarts occurred at 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z, 2026-03-22T21:59:47Z and 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z, each at the end of a ~1-day ramp. Consumer lag spiked only within the hour of each OOM (lag flat ~56-65 msg otherwise), so lag spikes coincide with/follow the OOM rather than preceding it. Concurrent services checked (order-service) show flat stable memory, so this looks notification-service-specific — but the co-tenant scope check was cut short by the tool budget.

events.statement: In the post-maintenance window (2026-03-23T16:00–23:59Z), notification-service consumer_lag stays flat at ~52–67 msgs throughout the flat period and spikes ONLY at the OOM: 2026-03-23T19:30Z avg 3069.83/max 18137.93, 20:00Z avg 6004.47/max 14213.61, then back to avg 57.18 at 20:30Z. Importantly the 18:00Z bucket (right at the Kafka retention change, 18:00:00Z) shows avg 64.6/max 75.74 — no lag response to the maintenance itself. Lag rises only in the ~30 min bucket containing the 19:59:21Z OOM, i.e. after/with the memory exhaustion, not at the change time.

notification-service memory_pct was already in a monotonic ramp well BEFORE the 18:00Z maintenance: 2026-03-23T14:00Z avg 83.82, climbing continuously (16:30Z 89.12, 17:45Z 93.37, 19:00Z 96.17, max 98.44 at 19:25Z) and only dropping at the 19:50Z bucket (avg 66.53) into 20:15Z (avg 47.2) — the restart reset. So the last ~4h pre-OOM is a steady climb with no inflection at 18:00Z.

notification-service logs in the maintenance window (18:00–21:00Z) show a GC/heap-pressure signature leading the OOM, NOT rebalance or partition-assignment activity: 10 WARN 'heap usage N% over 90 (old gen), full GC took Nms' lines from 18:34:46Z (4152ms) escalating to 19:49:28Z (6488ms), then one ERROR 'container notification-service-7d9f OOMKilled (exit code 137), restarting' at 19:59:21Z. Full-GC pause duration grows monotonically (4152→6488ms) toward the kill.

No rebalance or partition-assignment events exist in notification-service logs for the whole 2026-03-23T14:00–23:59Z window: searches for 'rebalance' and 'partition' both returned total_matched 0 (returned 0, truncated false). The same 'rebalance' search on the co-sharer settlement-service also returned 0 matches. There is no log evidence of a rebalance storm or partition reassignment around the maintenance/OOM.

notification-service request_rate (consumer throughput proxy) is flat with no replay surge: ~130–142 req/s across 14:00–23:59Z, dipping slightly to avg 128.67 at 21:20Z (post-restart) and never exceeding max 152.2. There is no throughput spike that would indicate an unusually large replay volume crossing the maintenance or the OOM.

Interpretation: the OOM correlates with heap/old-gen saturation (an internal memory ramp, already at ~84% by 14:00Z and rising to ~98% by 19:25Z) reaching a limit, not with replay volume or a traffic/rebalance shift. Lag spikes at 19:30–20:00Z are temporally downstream of near-full heap rather than at the 18:00Z retention change, and throughput is flat — consistent with the 'choking on a replay' theory being unsupported in this window.

events.description: No broker-side/consumer-group telemetry is exposed: the only metrics available for notification-service are consumer_lag, cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts — there are no per-consumer fetch, partition-assignment, or broker rebalance metrics. So I could not directly measure partition assignment counts or per-consumer fetch rates.
No JVM heap/RSS byte-level gauges (only a memory_pct percentage) and no Kafka broker service in the metric set; heap evidence is limited to GC WARN log lines.

No rebalance logs located for notification-service or settlement-service in the incident window even though a historical precedent (HIST-104) involved a broker-rebalance cause; log retention/verbosity may simply not emit rebalance events.

events.answer: Zooming into the maintenance→OOM window, the data does NOT support a large-replay or rebalance/traffic-shift cause. Consumer lag is flat (~52–67 msgs) right through the 18:00:00Z Kafka retention change and spikes only in the single bucket containing the 19:59:21Z OOM (avg 3069→6004, max ~18k), while notification-service throughput (request_rate) is flat (~130–142 req/s) with no replay surge, and no rebalance/partition log events exist service-side. Instead, memory_pct was already ramping monotonically from ~84% at 14:00Z to ~98% by 19:25Z with escalating old-gen full-GC pauses (4152ms→6488ms), i.e. the OOM correlates with internal heap saturation, not message volume or a rebalance. The reported "choking on a replay right after Kafka maintenance" theory is not visible in this window.

Shared-component resource contention reduced memory available to notification-service
Email-provider / downstream slowdown caused unbounded in-memory queueing of unsent notifications
